column2: On the authority of Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Allah the Exalted has laid down obligations, so do not neglect them;

He has set limits, so do not overstep them; He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy to you, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search into them.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by al-Dāraquṭnī and others.
Faraḍa (“has laid down”): has made obligatory and binding. “So do not neglect them”: by leaving them or being careless about them.

“So do not overstep them”: do not go beyond them. “So do not violate them”: do not engage in them or approach them. “And He has remained silent about things”: He has not ruled on them in any way. “Out of mercy for you”: by not making them unlawful or lawful.
“Not out of forgetfulness”: of their rulings. “So do not search into them”: do not probe and ask about them.
Allah the Exalted has laid down obligations and commanded that they be kept.
Allah the Exalted has forbidden things, so it is not permissible to engage in them or approach them.
Allah has set limits, so it is not permissible to overstep them.
When He, Glorified is He, has remained silent about things, they are not to be searched into and asked about, out of mercy for His servants, because they are lawful.
This hadith divides the rulings of the religion into four categories: obligations, prohibitions, limits and what is passed over in silence.

This hadith guides us to the fact that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, has laid obligations upon us and bound us to carry them out and keep them; so we should not contravene the commands of Allah by leaving them or being careless about them and so bring deficiency

and defect into them and not perform them fully. Allah, Glorified is He, has set limits and commanded us not to go beyond them and overstep them into what is not lawful or permissible for us to commit; and He has forbidden us things, so it is not permissible for us to engage in them or approach them.
He has remained silent about things, mentioning no ruling for them, whether lawful or unlawful—not out of forgetting to explain their rulings,

for our Lord, Glorified is He, neither errs nor forgets. So their ruling is not to be searched into, because Allah, Glorified is He, is All-Wise, All-Knowing, putting things in their proper places: “He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned” [al-Anbiyāʾ 21:23]. He does not leave anything except for a wise reason.
A man is only where he places himself, / so place yourself among righteous deeds.
Matters and deeds have an outcome, / so fear a sudden recompense and beware of it in good time.
The man of sense leaves what he craves, fearing / a hateful remedy for the harm it brings.
It is part of manliness for a man to leave his craving; / so look to which of the two you have preferred, and take heed.
